result.title: Joint Latent Reasoning and Observation for Agentic Video Understanding
result.summary: Effective video agents must learn not only how to answer, but also where to look next. Transferring this capability to smaller models is challenging because each observation serves two purposes: supporting an answer and guiding the search for further evidence. Textual descriptions may capture what is currently visible while omitting cues needed for subsequent acquisition. We introduce Latent Agentic Reasoning for Video Analysis (LARVA), a framework that distills multi-round video agents through jointly learned latent reasoning and visual observations. Rather than communicating through captions, an observer passes compact continuous representations to a reasoner that selects the next acquisition action or produces the final answer. Crucially, action and answer supervision propagate through this interface, training the observer to communicate information useful for downstream decisions. Observation reconstruction and reasoning-distribution alignment provide auxiliary supervision from textual teacher trajectories. Across five video-understanding benchmarks, LARVA achieves strong performance with 4B and 7B backbones. On VideoHolmes, Video-MME, and LVBench, the 7B model outperforms a textual CoT student trained on the same teacher trajectories by 5.1, 2.5, and 3.7 percentage points, respectively. These results highlight the value of jointly learning how agents represent evidence and act on it when distilling video-understanding capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LARVA，把多轮视频 agent 蒸馏成「observer 向 reasoner 传递紧凑连续表示」的框架：reasoner 依据该 latent 选择下一步观察动作或给出答案，动作与答案监督反向穿过这一接口，并以观察重建和推理分布对齐作为辅助监督；在五个视频基准上用 4B/7B 骨干评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及 latent 表示承载视觉证据并驱动 LOOK/STOP 决策与作答，动作监督回传视觉接口可供核查 latent 是否真被使用、是否信息坍缩；与同轨迹文本 CoT 学生的对比也为视觉旁路与内容保真提供线索。
